docs.summary: How one character is to be laid out. It arrives filled in from the layout settings, and a [`GlyphCustomizer`](#api~Prowl.Scribe.GlyphCustomizer) may change any of it. Whatever comes back is what Scribe shapes, kerns, measures, wraps and places with, so a character given a different font or size is a real part of the layout rather than something stretched afterwards. This is the hook for layout. Its counterpart at draw time is [`GlyphModifier`](#api~Prowl.Scribe.GlyphModifier), which moves and recolours the finished quad without disturbing where anything sits.
Index of this character in the string being laid out.

The character to lay out, already combined from a surrogate pair where there was one. Replace it and Scribe shapes, measures and draws the replacement, which is all a password field masked with asterisks needs. [`CharIndex`](#api~Prowl.Scribe.GlyphStyle~CharIndex) still points at the real character, so hit testing and selection keep working on the text as typed.
Null falls back to the layout's own font, which then searches the fallbacks.
Zero or less falls back to the layout's pixel size.
Extra width after this character. Ignored for spaces, which use WordSpacing.
Extra width after this character when it is a space.
Draw a line under this character. Neighbours that are also underlined share one bar.
Draw a line through this character.
